title: Calculating the Goodwill Relief on a Personal Checking Account
content:
The goodwill relief is the charges in the relief pool taken at the goodwill share and rounded half-up to the cent, held down to the shortfall standing on the account and to the episode ceiling, whichever of the three is smallest.

The goodwill relief is worked out only after every temporary credit owed on a claim still being looked into stands posted to the account.

**The relief window** is the standard relief window of 1 calendar month.

**The relief pool** is the largest single overdraft charge standing on the Personal Checking account.

**The goodwill share** is the modest relief share of 0.3.

**The shortfall standing on the account.** The money by which the account's own entries leave it below zero is every debit posted to the account — paid items, charges and take-back entries — less every credit posted to it — deposits, refunds and goodwill entries, temporary credits, surcharge rebates and interest credits — rounded half-up to the cent and never taken below zero. The shortfall standing on the account is half, that is 0.5, of the money by which the account's own entries leave it below zero.

**The episode ceiling** is the tight episode ceiling of 80.00.

The goodwill relief is taken in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up.

**Worked example on hypothetical inputs.** An account carries overdraft charges of 35.00, 35.00 and 30.00, and its own entries leave it 180.00 below zero.

| Quantity | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Relief pool | 35.00 |
| Relief pool taken at the goodwill share, rounded half-up to the cent | 10.50 |
| Money by which the account's entries leave it below zero | 180.00 |
| Shortfall standing on the account | 90.00 |
| Episode ceiling | 80.00 |
| Smallest of the three | 10.50 |
| Goodwill relief, in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up | 10.00 |

Where the account's entries left it 12.00 below zero, the shortfall standing would be 6.00 and that, being the smallest of the three, would be the figure carried into the final rounding. An account whose credits match or exceed its debits leaves the money below zero at 0.00, the figure never being taken below zero.
